newsitem.title: USA: Ohio voters back 17 school bond issues, reject 25.
newsitem.headline: Ohio voters back 17 school bond issues, reject 25.

text.p: Ohio voters approved 17 school bond issues and rejected 25 others in the special election Tuesday, according to unofficial election results.
Among the results from the larger issues, voters approved separate school district proposals seeking nearly $50.68 million of bonds and $32 million of bonds, election officials said Wednesday.
But voters in other school districts also rejected numerous other referendums, including requests for $42.93 million of bonds, $33.5 million and $31 million, election officials said.

In the greater Cincinnati area, voters in the Oak Hills Local School District approved nearly $50.67 million of bonds for a new middle school, plus renovation and additional classrooms for other schools.
Nearby, in the Lebanon City Schools District in Warren County voters rejected a proposed $31 million of bonds.

In Summit County, which includes Akron, Ohio, and surrounding areas, voters overwhelmingly approved one bond request, narrowly defeated another and overwhelmingly voted down a third, election officials said.
Residents voted 3,041 to 798 to approve $32 million of bonds for the Barberton City School District over a 25 year period.
Residents in the Nordonia Hills School District voted 2,857 for and 2,898 against a proposal for $33.5 million of school construction bonds over a 30-year period.
And in the Tallmadge City School District, residents rejected a request for $25 million of bonds voting 1,017 for and 4,753 against, election officials said.
In Cuyahoga County, encompassing Cleveland and surrounding communities, residents supported two school bond proposals and rejected one other, election officials said.
Voters in the Chagrin Falls School Distict voted 710 to 458 to approve $21.8 million of bonds for site improvements over a 25-year period, election officials said.

Voters in the Westlake City School District approved $7.25 million of bonds for the public library, while voters in the Maple Heights City School District rejected a request for $13.5 million of bonds, Cuyahoga County election officials said.
